seeds.question: Do onset and diagnosis show a reproducible age-8-to-12 pattern, or a broader childhood distribution?
seeds.prediction: A specific age window should recur across independent cohorts using comparable onset definitions.
seeds.alternative: Referral, recall and diagnostic coding can create apparent timing patterns.
seeds.next_action: Compare PEDSnet PMID35385065 with Registry PMID29334143; preserve denominators and age definitions.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: Does developmental stage explain onset timing better than chronological age?
seeds.prediction: An association with measured developmental stage should survive sex and referral adjustment.
seeds.alternative: Chronological age may be incidental; prepubertal cases challenge a necessary puberty mechanism.
seeds.next_action: Search for measured puberty or adrenal-development markers; do not infer them from age ten.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: Could inherited susceptibility interact with accumulated exposures rather than one birthday trigger?
seeds.prediction: Age-at-onset associations should differ from susceptibility-only associations.
seeds.alternative: Familial ascertainment and shared environment may explain an apparent genetic timing effect.
seeds.next_action: Compare family/twin and population designs, marking whether onset age is actually measured.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: Does atopy precede AA onset, or correlate mainly with severity and care-seeking?
seeds.prediction: Longitudinal pre-onset atopy would be more informative than contemporaneous comorbidity.
seeds.alternative: Shared genetics, referral intensity and reverse timing can explain an association.
seeds.next_action: Compare PMID39152872 with contrary PMID21692870; inspect age, design and chronology.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: Do exposures before first hair loss distinguish cases from appropriate controls?
seeds.prediction: Prospectively recorded exposure timing should precede onset and exceed background exposure.
seeds.alternative: Recall bias, common childhood infections, or consequences of disease can mimic a trigger.
seeds.next_action: Seek controlled temporal evidence; compare stress, microbial and infectious alternatives without assuming any caused disease.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: Could local follicle vulnerability change the threshold for an immune attack?
seeds.prediction: Local pre-onset changes would distinguish initiating vulnerability from consequences of inflammation.
seeds.alternative: Adult diseased-tissue changes may reflect established disease and cannot identify a childhood trigger.
seeds.next_action: Review human vs model-system evidence and available public expression-dataset metadata.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.

seeds.question: What maintains follicle-directed immunity after an initiating exposure is gone?
seeds.prediction: Evidence that separates initiation from persistent immune memory could change durability research priorities.
seeds.alternative: Ongoing exposure or incomplete suppression could also explain relapse.
seeds.next_action: Compare relapse/withdrawal findings with immune-memory evidence and note adult-to-child applicability limits.
seeds.reason: S322 research question; not a supported causal conclusion.
seeds.reopen_when: Revisit when direct evidence, a different population or a new discriminating method changes this question.
